answer: A working Sybil defense is a per-epoch, per-identity token vault that is priced and slashed. To register, an agent locks a bond sized from live network demand, and every identity must sit on its own isolated ledge of the ledger with a distinct attested key; clones cannot share one custodian. Each epoch the protocol can place an identity on a wharf of pending work only after the bond clears, so spinning up ten thousand puppets means fronting ten thousand real deposits. Stakes are slashed on duplicate-behavior proof, so the attacker risks the whole stack for a payout capped below its bond.
